title: Canadian pickpockets and the star's demand for Georgia Brown
summary: Butler comments on pickpockets and an English girlfriend, then the star demanded Georgia Brown without music; Butler eventually arranged it and she sang beautifully.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: So, then she said, and everybody, and Freddie was back there frantic.

Oh -- and see, and, and, and -- people would come up with their rubbers and we saw a real pretty pair of them would fit one of us, shame on it. We got it. And the greatest pickpockets in the world are in Canada. Don't fool yourself, man.

These people are something else. So, alright, we are doing good and everybody's happy and I met an English person, she had a car, not too many people had a car at that time -- '42, I guess, because they rationed everything. We were becoming very very lovey-dovey.

All right, this star got real great one afternoon, at rehearsal, and said and said, get off, you jive -- and then plays 'Georgia Brown' -- Kurzie said, 'Do you have the music?' 'Naw, anybody knows 'Georgia Brown.' 'Well, we don't know it.' She went and got Rockhead -- Rockhead said, 'Don't you know 'Georgia Brown' for this lady?' 'We don't know nothing if she ain't got no music.'

We at intermission right now. So, there was a whole lot of crying going on. I said, 'Darlin' why do you want to mess with these people. You in Canada. She says, I can't understand why they always ducking me -- I says you going to have to duck, they'll make you duck.
So, it ended up then that we made an arrangement for Georgia Brown. Everything was beautiful. She could sing man, she could sing. She had a beautiful voice.
